issues.legal_issue: Temporary unlawfulness of contractual performance does not discharge a contract by frustration where the unlawful period is temporary and performance was not required by a specified time.
material_facts: The purchaser contracted to buy plots after the seller completed development work, including roads and drains, and agreed to complete the purchase within a month after that work was completed.
The government requisitioned the land, depriving the seller of access and making development work unlawful during the requisition.
The contract did not specify a time for completing the development work, although it made time essential for completing the sale after that work was done.
The parties entered the contract while aware of wartime circumstances and the possibility of difficulties, including requisition of the land.
issues.conclusion: The contract was not discharged by frustration because the requisition made development unlawful only temporarily, and the contract did not require that development be completed within a specified time.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 56 and 32 of the Contract Act, frustration is assessed under the Act rather than by implying a fundamental term as English courts do. Supervening impossibility or unlawfulness can discharge a contract, and impossibility includes impracticability caused by an event for which neither party is responsible. But temporary unlawfulness does not itself discharge the contract: discharge may follow where time is essential or a performance deadline is specified and the unlawfulness exists when performance is due. Section 46's reasonable-time requirement did not alter the result because the parties knew of the prevailing circumstances and intended that time consumed by material shortages or requisition would not count against development. The Court relied on Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. for the relevant approach to frustration and on Denny Mott & Dickson Ltd. v. James B. Fraser & Co. Ltd. in considering the effect of temporary unlawfulness.

rule.if: land_sale_contract_with_development_obligation and temporary_unlawfulness_of_development and development_deadline_unspecified and parties_aware_of_disruption

predicates.land_sale_contract_with_development_obli: The parties made a contract for the sale of land under which the seller was to complete development work before the purchaser completed the sale.
predicates.temporary_unlawfulness_of_development: A supervening event made the seller's development work unlawful for a temporary period.
predicates.development_deadline_unspecified: The contract did not specify when the seller had to complete the development work.
predicates.parties_aware_of_disruption: When contracting, the parties knew of circumstances that made disruption to the development work foreseeable.

issues.definition: When a land-sale contract requires development before completion, a temporary legal bar to development does not discharge the contract by frustration if no development deadline was specified and the parties were aware of possible disruption.

issues.legal_issue: A specific-performance suit that is premature when filed may be considered in light of subsequent events that occur before the appeal is heard.
material_facts: The purchaser filed a suit for specific performance before the seller had completed the development work that triggered the purchaser's right to obtain a conveyance.
The development work had been completed by the time the appeal was heard by the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The premature-suit contention failed because the court could take account of the later completion of the development work when moulding relief.
issues.legal_principle: A court may take notice of events occurring after a suit is filed and mould its relief accordingly; the Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this proposition.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A claimant brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.development_incomplete_when_suit_filed: The development work required before the claimant could obtain a conveyance was unfinished when the proceeding was filed.
predicates.development_complete_before_appeal_heard: The required development work was completed before the appeal was heard.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit filed before required development is complete, the court may consider that development's completion before the appeal is heard when moulding relief.
